title: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
lede: A case study estimates that Anthropic's contracted U.S. data centers will draw about 87% of their power from gas and 11% from coal in 2028, emitting around 32 million tonnes of CO2 in its mid case.

points: Anthropic's only disclosed renewable commitments are in Norway and Canada, while it has bought commitments for 1.7 GW of gas generators.
Of 15 GW of contracted compute, 5.9 to 9.6 GW is tied to named sites, mostly on grids where new load is met by marginal gas and coal plants.
The 2028 range of 17 to 38 million tonnes could exceed the emissions of all power generation in California, the authors say.
About a quarter of the power is on-site gas, and 80% of that runs on simple cycle turbines and engines that pollute more than combined cycle plants.
Air pollution damages are put at $2 to 3 billion a year, and the study notes Colossus 2 still runs largely on unpermitted turbines.

points.text: Calls for regulation recur across the thread: without rules, commenters say, the pollution costs fall on communities far from the people deciding.
One commenter argues that gas produced alongside US shale oil would otherwise be flared, so generating power from it can make sense.
Some point to small local models on rooftop solar as a way to opt out of the large providers' energy choices.
Others expect cost pressure to help, since providers pay directly for power and inference is already getting much cheaper.
